patch_description:
The original implementation failed validation because it could alter dataframe structure and row/value placement while recursively rebuilding frames. It added an `original_index` column, merged/dropped columns, used positional assignment with `as_completed()` (which loses the source row position), and finally returned an empty `column_orderings` list. Those behaviors violate the required preservation and per-row ordering contract.

The replacement keeps every original row, column, cell value, index, and shape intact. It only permutes existing cell positions within each row and returns the corresponding per-row source-column order. It evaluates a bounded set of deterministic column-order candidates using the actual serialized-row Trie objective: lexicographically sorted LCP character reuse. It supports mixed types and missing values without modifying stored values, includes a frequency-ranked global order, a conditional grouping order, and preserves supplied merge/dependency ordering constraints.
